we identified amide and thioamide derivatives, of which antagonists activities were highly enhanced in the multiple H-bonds.
the incorporation of cyano- or vinyl-substituents to the multiple H- bonding region of diaryl alkyl (thio)-amides resulted in the potent and selective antagonists of TRPV1.
the incorporation of a cyano group to the multiple H- bonding region of amide and thioamide derivatives resulted in potent antagonists of the TRPV1 channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel class of TRPV1 antagonistic agents that are based on the multiple H-bonds.

structural optimization of multiple hydrogen bonding region in the diarylalkylamide/thioamide series as novel TRPV(1) antagonists, and the present work is the first to identify potent TRPV(1)-selective antagonists with multiple hydrogen bonding region.
the structural optimization of multiple hydrogen bonding region in diarylalkylamides as novel vanilloid receptor antagonists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a cyano-substituted diarylalkylamide/thioamide with a multiple H-bonded structure is an effective TRPV1 antagonist, and that the cyano-substituent in a multiple H-bonds region is an effective substituent to enhance TRPV1 antagonistic activity.
multiple H-bondings are essential for the TRPV1 antagonistic activity and the cyano or vinyl groups are effective for enhancing the TRPV1 inhibitory activity.
a combination of multiple H-bonds with the appropriate substituents on the amide/thioamide moiety can provide potent TRPV1 antagonistic activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of a cyano or vinyl group in the multiple H-bonds is an efficient strategy for the improvement of antagonistic potency.

a combination of the multiple H-bonds with a proper substitution of the multiple H-Bonding region would be a useful strategy to obtain a novel series of TRPV1 antagonistic compounds with high affinity.
the introduction of a cyano or vinyl group at the 3-position of the multiple H-bonds of the amide/thioamide moiety is a key structural element for the enhancement of the TRPV1 antagonist activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multiple H-bonds in amides/thioamide are essential to the TRPV1 antagonist activities, and that the multiple H bonds can be enhanced by the introduction of a cyano or a vinyl group.
multiple H-bond acceptors are important for potent antagonists, and a combination of multiple H-bonds is more important than the number of H-bonds.
the incorporation of electron-withdrawing group into the multiple H-bonds region of diaryl alkyl amides/thiomides can significantly improve TRPV1 antagonistic activity.
